feature: Delete over a marquee says why it did nothing
summary: Backspace with a marquee up still takes the piece out of a picture and says nothing about it, because nothing needs saying. Over a shape or a piece of text there is no bitmap for the hole to go in, so instead of the key going quiet, one line at the bottom of the canvas says a piece can only be taken out of a picture and that clearing the marquee deletes the whole layer.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. "Say when a piece cannot be taken out" is on by default, and so is "Copy takes the layer you picked", which decides that a marquee keeps the layer you picked.

try.do: Open a new document and drag a screenshot in from the Finder.
Press V and click the picture to pick it.
Press M and drag a marquee over one corner of it.
Press Command Z, then Escape, then draw a rectangle with R.
Press V, click the rectangle, press M and drag a marquee over its left half.
Press Escape to clear the marquee, then Backspace again.

evaluate: Is a refusal what you want here, or would you rather Backspace deleted the whole shape and let undo sort it out?
Does the line reach you at the bottom of the canvas, or were you still looking at the marquee?
Does "Only a picture can have a piece taken out" say enough, given a rectangle on screen looks like a picture?
The line stays up after Escape clears the marquee, so it is still there while you do what it says. Right, or should it go with the marquee?
Deleting a corner out of a picture says nothing at all. Is that the right amount of nothing?
rough: Nothing new was built for this. The refusal landed on 2026-09-07 with the cut task, which covered Backspace as well as Command X, so this run reproduced it on the probe and covered the half that walk never pressed: Backspace over a marquee on a real picture, which must stay silent.

The Experiments switch was called "Say when a piece cannot be cut out" and now reads "Say when a piece cannot be taken out", since it governs Backspace too and the old name sent you looking for the wrong key.
Option Backspace, which fills the marquee, is still silent over a shape. It has its own task and was left alone here.
A picture that has been cropped or turned gets a different line ("This picture is cropped or turned"). No walk can reach that state yet, so it is covered by tests rather than by a screenshot.
How long the line hangs around is three seconds, decided and tested in the model. A walk cannot time it, because a walk's wait ends as soon as the app goes quiet.
Screen Recording was granted, so both screenshots here are real window captures.
